notes: Ash resources participating in queues MUST be built on Ash 3.x, using Ash.Tracer and :telemetry for observability, per Ash 3 monitoring guidance.
Ash 2.x patterns/APIs MUST NOT be used anywhere in this suite.

capability_signatures.description: Defines a trigger for an Ash resource action that enqueues Oban jobs.
Defines a scheduled action for recurring Oban jobs.
Builds the generated trigger worker job arguments before Oban insertion.

notes: AshOban extension MUST support triggers and scheduled actions for Ash 3.x resources.
CI tasks MUST verify capability signatures (module, function, arity) against loaded code to prevent behavioral drift or incompatible forks.
Triggers and scheduled actions MUST define explicit worker_module_name and scheduler_module_name to avoid dangling jobs when names change, per AshOban documentation.
CI MUST verify the selected AshOban generated-argument capability profile against the exact loaded package version and generated-worker behavior; an unprofiled version MUST fail closed.

best_practices: Side-effectful workflows (e.g. emails, notifications) MUST be modelled as Ash resources with ash_oban triggers, not ad-hoc Oban workers.
Use Ash multi-step actions / Reactor for orchestration and AshOban to execute durable steps asynchronously where appropriate.
Use AshOban's VerifyModuleNames and capability checks to ensure all triggers and scheduled actions have stable module names and expected signatures.

notes: Jobs triggered off fresh writes MUST either carry a safe payload subset or read from primary to avoid replica lag issues.
Lag-aware strategies MAY inspect replication metrics before executing heavy reads.

capability_profile.source_observation: AshOban.run_trigger/3 calls build_trigger/3 then Oban.insert!/1; build_trigger/3 creates the listed keys and filters those reserved keys from extra_args and :args.

scheduler_control_job.purpose: Framework-generated control job that enumerates tenants and schedules tenant-bound trigger jobs; it MUST NOT perform a Ticketing domain mutation or external side effect.
scheduler_control_job.compatibility: The payload-free generated argument shape MUST remain readable across the current and immediately previous deployed application versions; stable scheduler_module_name is required.

framework_key_values.metadata: Safe, non-sensitive framework metadata only; no Ticketing business payload.
framework_key_values.action_arguments: Ticketing-controlled job input MUST exist only in the nested ticketing_payload object.
framework_key_values.tenant: Must be established before tenant-scoped Ash access; where duplicated as org_id in ticketing_payload.args, values MUST match or the job MUST fail closed.
framework_key_values.actor: Optional. Persist only the minimal AUTH-030 tuple plus evaluated_at_utc when actor context is required; otherwise set actor_persister to :none or equivalent.

shared_rules.size_accounting: Count the complete persisted Oban job args map, including all framework keys and the nested ticketing_payload, against max_args_bytes.
shared_rules.security: No raw PII, bearer tokens, or full permission snapshots in any framework or Ticketing payload field.

capability_verification.drift_rule: A package version or generated argument profile not listed by a verified capability signature MUST fail CI until authority is updated.

notes: Release-hygiene bump: two separately distributed OBQC-1@2.1.6 bundles were byte-identical; issuing 2.1.7 to remove ambiguity and provide a single canonical reference for downstream suite pins.
Patched for CI lockability and dependency alignment.

changes: Added runtime_policy requirements for topology via admission controllers (e.g. OPA/Gatekeeper).
Switched Ash/AshOban requirements from explicit SemVer to capability-based assertions.
Introduced PSC-1 latency profile integration so pointer-based jobs use HEAVY instead of violating STANDARD budgets.
Clarified Ash 3.x observability requirements referencing Ash.Tracer and :telemetry.
MAJOR: Added break-glass annotation requirements for runtime admission policies to allow controlled overrides during SEV1 incidents.
MAJOR: Introduced capability_signatures and CI verification to prevent AshOban capability hallucinations.
MAJOR: Added HEAVY latency profile quotas to prevent HEAVY from becoming the default profile.
MAJOR: Introduced an Ash 2.x observability deprecation window with a grace period to avoid blocking critical hotfixes while migrating to Ash 3.x.
MINOR: Added traffic_shaping model with explicit job classes (polling vs recovery vs ingress vs cpu_batch) and required retry profiles.
MINOR: Aligned queue taxonomy to canonical foundation queue names and added compute isolation metadata for cpu_intensive workloads.
MINOR: Enforced snooze semantics for polling jobs and forbade blocking sleep in polling workers.
MINOR: Increased absolute job argument cap to 8192 bytes with a recommended default target of 2048 bytes and strengthened payload hygiene notes.
PATCH: Normalized contract envelope schema_version to contract-suite/1.0 for CS-0@2.2.0 compliance.

change_log.summary: Patch: fix stale gate version pins; bump version for release hygiene. No semantic changes.

changes: MINOR: Preserve the exact version/args wrapper for standard Oban workers and define an allowlisted AshOban framework envelope with a versioned Ticketing payload.
MINOR: Define a safe, payload-free AshOban scheduler control-job exception and compatibility evidence from the prior deployed source commit, removing the unavailable planned ART-0 dependency.
MINOR: Require fail-closed payload version and tenant checks, full persisted-args size accounting, and capability-profile drift gates.

concurrency_math.description: Worker concurrency is derived from DB pool size and deployment topology, not naked integers.
notes: API must retain at least api_reserve_fraction * db_max_connections connections globally.
Workers MUST NOT be scaled horizontally without re-validating global_formula via CI and runtime admission policies.
PSC-1 connection_leasing invariants apply to both API and worker connections.
Priority alone does not guarantee fast dispatch; partial indexes on available jobs are required.
Large tables MUST be partitioned by state and inserted_at to avoid bloat and vacuum contention.

required_indexes.name: oban_jobs_available_priority_index
required_indexes.rationale: Enables fast retrieval of highest-priority available jobs without scanning the entire table.

verification.description: Verify required indexes against actual DB schema (pg_catalog/structure.sql), not just code or resource definitions.

dependencies.reason: Connection leasing, latency budgets, and latency profiles for worker/API coexistence.
Atomic updates and advisory locks for dedupe and idempotency.
Error codes for job failures, DLQ, and retry exhaustion.
Queue depth/lag metrics, alerting, and runbooks for OBQC backpressure + circuit breaker actions.

standard_oban_worker.applies_to: Oban workers not generated by AshOban.

ash_oban_generated_worker.compatibility_requirement: Current and immediately previous semantic Ticketing payload versions MUST be accepted during rolling deployment.

compatibility_evidence.description: CI MUST replay the current and immediately previous deployed versioned payload fixtures against current workers. The previous fixture MUST be sourced from the exact prior deployed application source commit and carry that immutable commit SHA and fixture digest; do not infer it from a planned registry.
fixture_requirements: Fixtures MUST be sanitized, contain no raw PII, bearer tokens, or permission snapshots, and cover the exact persisted payload shape.
The prior deployed source commit SHA and fixture digest MUST be recorded with CI evidence.
The previous deployed fixture MUST remain available to the next release compatibility check.
compatibility_evidence.first_deployment: When no earlier worker deployment and no queued legacy jobs exist, test and record the initial payload version and sanitized fixture as the compatibility baseline. Every later deployment MUST test that actual prior deployed fixture as N-1.
compatibility_evidence.incompatible_change: Drain or transform old jobs before activation, or provide an explicitly versioned migration worker that preserves the prior behavior.

notes: Standard Oban workers MUST use the exact two-key version/args wrapper.
AshOban-generated resource action workers use only the exact framework outer-key allowlist and keep Ticketing-controlled inputs under action_arguments.ticketing_payload.

AshOban-generated scheduler control jobs are the sole payload-free exception because the framework creates those control jobs without Ticketing action inputs; their arguments MUST match the certified profile and they MUST have no domain or external side effects.
Workers MUST handle the current and immediately previous semantic payload versions during rolling deploys, except the first deployment with no prior worker version or queued jobs.
Deploys that introduce incompatible argument shapes MUST drain or transform old jobs or provide an explicitly versioned migration worker.

foundation_refs.reason: V42 is the constitutional foundation for queue correctness, idempotent side effects, tenant isolation, and payout-safe backpressure behavior.

notes: Locked for repo commit; status remains 'active' per CS schema.
Job arguments MUST NOT exceed max_args_bytes (absolute cap).
Default job classes MUST target <= recommended_default_max_args_bytes by passing stable identifiers, not full structs/blobs.
Oversized payloads MUST use pointer_plus_primary_read and MUST bind to PSC-1 latency profiles.
PSC-1 MUST define latency profiles (e.g. STANDARD, HEAVY) for worker queues.
No more than heavy_quota_fraction (e.g. 0.2) of workers or traffic in a given domain MAY use the HEAVY latency profile without an explicit architectural review.
Quota breaches MUST surface as P1 incidents and trigger review of payload sizing and workflow design, not silent profile changes.

queues.description: Latency-sensitive ingress and provider callbacks (e.g., webhooks).
queues.name: integrations

queues.description: User communications (email/SMS/push) isolated from money path.
queues.name: notifications

notes: Jobs in compliance queue MUST execute only on cpu_intensive node pools to prevent starvation of ingress/finance work.

queues.description: Ticket issuance and inventory-related background work.
queues.name: tickets

rules.text: OBQC-1 and OBQC-1-GATE MUST be JSON-only normative artifacts; repacks are forbidden; metadata must match filenames and manifest pins.
rules.title: GOVERNANCE - OBQC-1-META-001

rules.rationale: Prevents workers from starving API connections on a single node.
rules.text: Worker concurrency MUST be derived from DB pool size per node; static per-node limits without pool awareness are forbidden.
rules.title: CONCURRENCY - OBQC-1-CONCUR-001

rules.rationale: Prevents horizontal scaling from overwhelming the database while allowing carefully audited emergency overrides.
rules.text: Global worker concurrency across all nodes MUST respect DB max connections and API reserve, with both manifests and runtime admission controllers enforcing max_nodes and supporting controlled break-glass.
rules.title: CONCURRENCY - OBQC-1-CONCUR-002

rules.rationale: Avoids failures due to replica lag when processing hot data.
rules.text: Jobs triggered by fresh writes MUST use a replication-safe strategy (payload-in-args within limits or read-from-primary).
rules.title: REPLICATION - OBQC-1-REPL-001

rules.rationale: Prevents oban_jobs bloat, TOAST churn, and index degradation.
rules.text: Job argument payloads MUST respect max_args_bytes; oversized jobs MUST use pointer_plus_primary_read.
rules.title: PAYLOAD - OBQC-1-PAYLOAD-001

rules.rationale: Aligns replication-safe strategies with PSC-1 latency guarantees via explicit profiles and prevents HEAVY from becoming the default.
rules.text: Queues using pointer_plus_primary_read MUST be bound to an appropriate HEAVY latency profile defined in PSC-1, and HEAVY usage MUST respect per-domain quotas.
rules.title: LATENCY - OBQC-1-PSC-LAT-001

rules.rationale: Prevents stale or incompatible jobs across standard and AshOban framework-generated worker deployments.
rules.text: Standard Oban workers MUST use the exact version/args wrapper. AshOban-generated resource action workers MUST use the certified framework-aware allowlist and a versioned nested Ticketing payload; the payload-free scheduler control job is the only exception and MUST remain side-effect free. Current and immediately previous deployed payload versions MUST be compatible, with first-deployment baseline handling as specified by job_versioning.compatibility_evidence.
rules.title: VERSIONING - OBQC-1-VERSION-001

rules.rationale: Ensures high-priority jobs are dispatchable even under heavy backlog.
rules.text: oban_jobs MUST have a partial index on available jobs ordered by priority and scheduled_at, as verified against the real DB schema.
rules.title: DATABASE - OBQC-1-INDEX-001

rules.rationale: Prevents Ash 2.x drift and aligns with Ash 3.x-only project constitution.
rules.text: Ash resources participating in AshOban MUST use Ash 3.x patterns and terminology (Domains, not APIs). Ash 2.x patterns/APIs MUST NOT be used.
rules.title: FRAMEWORK - OBQC-1-ASH3-001

rules.rationale: Prevents capability hallucinations from forks or incompatible implementations.
rules.text: AshOban capabilities MUST be verified via module/function/arity signatures against loaded code, not just module presence.
rules.title: CAPABILITIES - OBQC-1-ASH-CAP-002

rules.rationale: Prevents queue proliferation and ensures incident controls (pause/shedding) operate predictably.
rules.text: Queue names MUST be canonical and limited to: tickets, integrations, finance, scanning, notifications, exports, ops, compliance.
rules.title: QUEUES - OBQC-1-QUEUE-001

rules.rationale: Prevents workload coupling where polling or CPU batching starves ingress and money-path work.
rules.text: All background work MUST declare a traffic class (ingress, polling, recovery, cpu_batch, best_effort) with an explicit retry_profile and queue isolation requirements.
rules.title: TRAFFIC_SHAPING - OBQC-1-TS-001

rules.rationale: Avoids user-visible lag for polling and prevents retry storms during dependency outages.
rules.text: Polling workloads MUST use linear_or_fixed retry schedules; recovery workloads MUST use exponential backoff with jitter. Library defaults MUST NOT be relied on.
rules.title: RETRIES - OBQC-1-BACKOFF-001

rules.rationale: Blocking sleeps exhaust worker pools and amplify latency under concurrent polling.
rules.text: Jobs waiting for external state changes MUST return {:snooze, seconds} and MUST NOT block worker processes (e.g., Process.sleep/1).
rules.title: POLLING - OBQC-1-SNOOZE-001

rules.rationale: Prevents CPU saturation from causing missed webhooks and scanning timeouts.
rules.text: CPU-heavy jobs MUST execute in dedicated queues and/or dedicated node pools and MUST NOT share worker pools with ingress queues.
rules.title: ISOLATION - OBQC-1-ISO-001

rules.rationale: Prevents cross-tenant leakage and ensures RLS/tenant scoping applies equally to synchronous and asynchronous execution.
rules.text: Any Oban job that reads or writes tenant-scoped resources MUST carry org_id (TEN-1 tenant_key) in args and MUST establish tenant context per TEN-1 before any Ash read/write. Jobs MUST fail fast if org_id is missing or invalid for the resource scope.
rules.title: TENANCY - Tenant context in background jobs

rules.rationale: Oban retries are expected; without idempotency, retries cause double charges, duplicate refunds, or seat over-allocation (V42 violations).
rules.text: All jobs in money-path (finance queue) and seat/inventory queues MUST be idempotent. Each execution MUST use a deterministic idempotency key derived from (org_id, domain, action, business_entity_id, job_version) and MUST enforce dedupe via LOCKS-1 before performing any external side-effect or ledger mutation.
rules.title: IDEMPOTENCY - Durable retries without double effects

rules.rationale: Prevents retry storms and protects money/inventory flows under provider instability, per V42 reliability requirements.
rules.text: Jobs that call external providers MUST use circuit breakers with thresholds: open on 5 consecutive failures OR >30% failures over 1 minute (minimum 20 calls). Cool-down MUST be 60 seconds. When open, non-critical operations MUST fail fast; critical safe-to-retry operations MUST be queued/retried.
rules.title: RELIABILITY - Circuit breakers for external dependencies

rules.statement: Job args MUST NOT include raw PII, bearer tokens, or full permission snapshots. Args MAY include stable ids (uuid_v7), identifier_hashes, and PSC-1 pointers. Sensitive data must be re-materialized at execution time after fresh authorization.
rules.title: No raw PII or permission snapshots in job args

rules.statement: For any job that can materialize PII or produce export artifacts, workers MUST perform a fresh IAM-1 decision_api authorization check at execution time. If the check denies OR liveness fails, the job MUST fail closed and MUST ensure any partial artifacts are deleted.
rules.title: Fresh authorization at execution time for sensitive jobs

rules.statement: If an actor context is required to execute a job, enqueue MUST record only (actor_kind,user_id,org_id,capability,resource_kind,resource_id,effective_permissions_hash_sha256) and evaluated_at_utc. Workers MUST compare the fresh effective_permissions_hash_sha256 with the recorded value; mismatch MUST deny (fail closed).
rules.title: Auth context is minimal + hash-bound
ASHOBAN - Framework-aware generated job arguments
rules.rationale: AshOban owns required transport keys; Ticketing controls a separate versioned payload and must reject unprofiled or unsafe argument shapes.
rules.text: AshOban-generated trigger and scheduled-action worker args MUST contain only the exact certified framework key allowlist and MUST place all Ticketing-controlled job input under action_arguments.ticketing_payload as a versioned {version, args} map. Reserved framework keys MUST NOT be replaced by extra_args or :args. Tenant disagreement between AshOban tenant and ticketing_payload.args.org_id MUST fail closed. Persisted actor data MUST satisfy AUTH-030; when actor persistence is unnecessary, actor_persister MUST be :none or equivalent. The complete persisted args map MUST respect max_args_bytes.

summary: Defines queue taxonomy, topology-aware concurrency, Ash 3.x AshOban integration, framework-aware and versioned job arguments, replication safety, payload limits, retry controls, and Oban database index requirements.
title: Oban Queue and Concurrency Contract

notes: For each worker deployment, HPA maxReplicas MUST NOT exceed V42_MAX_APP_NODES used in concurrency_math.
Runtime admission controllers MUST enforce the same max_nodes constraint for manual scale operations, except when an approved break-glass annotation is present.
Topology consistency checks MUST run in CI against the same manifests used for deploy, and runtime policies MUST be deployed from the same source of truth.
Admission policies MUST allow a controlled bypass when the break-glass annotation is present and matches the required format.
All break-glass uses MUST be logged, tied to an incident ID, and reviewed post-incident.
Break-glass MUST NOT be available in non-production environments without audit; policies MUST restrict usage to production namespaces with additional RBAC and audit.

runtime_policy.description: Cluster admission control (e.g. Gatekeeper/OPA) MUST reject scaling events that would violate concurrency_math.global_formula.

notes: CPU-heavy jobs MUST NOT execute on the same node pools as ingress queues.

job_classes.description: High-frequency state inquiry loops; must never block workers.
CPU-heavy batching; must be isolated from ingress queues.
Non-critical tasks that must degrade first during incidents.

notes: Polling jobs MUST return {:snooze, seconds} and MUST NOT block worker processes with Process.sleep/1.

profiles.name: polling
notes: Polling workloads MUST use fixed/linear schedules to avoid exponential status lag.

profiles.name: recovery
notes: Recovery workloads MUST use exponential backoff with jitter to avoid synchronized retry storms.
